name: Water flosser

lead: A water flosser, or oral irrigator, shoots a pulsing jet of water between teeth and along the gumline to flush out plaque and food debris. Countertop and cordless handheld versions are sold under brands such as Waterpik.
In appearance terms it is chiefly a gum-health tool, helpful for people with braces, implants or bridges, or who find string floss hard to use.

paras: Pulsed water pressure dislodges loosely attached plaque and bacteria from interdental spaces and shallow pockets, and the massaging action is thought to reduce gingival inflammation and bleeding.

Safety is good; excessive pressure can bruise gums and it should not be used straight after oral surgery. Systematic reviews show reliable improvements in gingival inflammation but inconsistent effects on plaque, and a recent meta-analysis found no extra benefit over regular floss for general patients. Many supporting trials are industry funded, so water flossers are a reasonable alternative to floss rather than a clear upgrade.
